title: Longest Repeating Substring
statement:
You are given a string `s`. A **repeating substring** is a contiguous piece of `s` that can be found in `s` at least twice, starting at two different positions; the two occurrences are allowed to overlap.

Return the length of the longest repeating substring of `s`, or `0` if no substring of `s` occurs more than once.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

A substring that repeats is a pair of occurrences ending at two different positions `i` and `j` that share a common ending. So the question becomes: over all pairs of end positions `i < j`, how long a suffix do the prefixes `s[0..i)` and `s[0..j)` have in common? That is the "common suffix" table familiar from longest-common-substring DP, applied to `s` against itself. Trying every length and every start with a set of seen pieces also works, but costs about O(n³).

## Approach

1. Let `curr[j]` (for the current `i`) be the length of the longest common suffix of `s[0..i)` and `s[0..j)`; only `j > i` matters, which keeps the two occurrences apart.
2. If `s[i - 1]` equals `s[j - 1]`, the common suffix extends the one for `(i - 1, j - 1)`, stored in `prev[j - 1]`, by one. Otherwise it is `0`.
3. Track the largest value ever stored in `best`.
4. After each row, the current row becomes `prev`; only two rows are kept.

## Example 1, step by step

For `s = "abcd"` no two positions hold the same letter, so the comparison `s[i - 1] === s[j - 1]` never succeeds, every cell stays `0`, and `best` stays `0`. In Example 2 (`"abbaba"`), the pair `i = 3`, `j = 5` matches `"ab"` ending at both, giving `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): every pair `i < j` is examined once.
- Space: O(n): only the previous and current rows are stored.

## Pitfalls

- Restrict to `j > i`; letting `j = i` would compare a position with itself and always report the whole prefix.
- Overlapping copies count (`"aaa"` has answer `2`), and the `i < j` table handles that without extra checks.
- When the letters differ, the cell must reset to `0`, not carry over the previous value: substrings are contiguous.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `s` |
| `i`, `j` | end positions (exclusive) of the two occurrences, `i < j` |
| `prev` | common-suffix lengths for row `i - 1` |
| `curr` | common-suffix lengths for row `i` |
| `best` | longest repeat found so far |

narration.2: Remember the length of the string.
narration.3: The previous DP row starts as all zeros: an empty prefix shares nothing.
narration.4: No repeat has been found yet.
narration.6: Choose the end of the first occurrence: the prefix s[0..i).
narration.7: Start a fresh row for this i.
narration.8: Only end positions j after i are paired, so the two occurrences start at different places.
narration.9: Do both prefixes end with the same letter?
narration.10: Yes: extend the common suffix of the two shorter prefixes by one.
narration.11: Keep the longest common suffix seen so far.
narration.14: This row becomes the previous row for the next i.
narration.16: The longest common suffix of any two different prefixes is the answer.
